label: Narrow corridor
note: one source (A); receiver positions 1, 3 and 4 at 2, 7 and 14 m (RIR_proforma/ReadMe.txt; no pro forma for this room); omni and SoundField at each position

label: Car cabin (Vauxhall Astra)
note: RIR pro forma 20150810_PP_04 (10 Aug 2015): one loudspeaker (a Genelec 8030A) in the front row, receiver 1 in the front passenger seat 0.6 m from it and receiver 2 in the rear middle seat 0.9 m from it; each seat measured twice (condition empty = first take, II = second take, 45-54 min later at the front seat and 9-21 min later at the rear). What changed between takes is not documented: the second takes decay faster (T20 of the omni 0.094 to 0.088 s front, 0.142 to 0.098 s rear), and at the rear seat the direct sound arrives 30 samples later (about 0.76 m from the source in the first take, 0.97 m in the second), so the microphone or the loudspeaker was probably moved there

label: Audio booth, Newton Building, University of Salford
note: one of the two reproduction rooms of the listening test, measured at the listening position from each of 16 loudspeakers (sources Spk_01-16): an octagon at 1.25 m and 8 more at 1.57 m, 4 at 38 degrees above and 4 at 38 degrees below the horizontal (Make_input_file_from_measured.m). rt_mid is empty for all 32 IRs: the 1 kHz decay fit fails where the noise floor is faded out. T30 is 0.08 s at 500 Hz and 0.07 s at 2 kHz, and 1 kHz read by hand is 0.07-0.08 s: a very dry booth.

label: Listening room, Newton Building, University of Salford
note: the other reproduction room, measured at the listening position from each of 16 loudspeakers (Spk_01-16): an octagon at 2.0 m, 4 at 2.1 m 25 degrees below and 4 at 2.2 m 25 degrees above the horizontal (Make_input_file_from_measured.m). rt_mid 0.25 s (8 of 32 IRs empty for the same reason), equal to ash_ir r03 and sbsbrir (0.25 s), both Salford's BS.1116 listening room.
